facts.text: Eberhardt Hall is the oldest building at NJIT and was built in 1857 as the Newark Orphan Asylum, a home for Newark's orphans.
When it opened, the Newark Orphan Asylum had gaslight, steam heat and hot-and-cold running water, which were rare even in the most affluent homes of the period.
The building was designed by architects John Welch and Thomas A. Roberts in Victorian and Elizabethan Gothic styles, drawing on 15th and 16th century castle design.
After the Newark College of Engineering acquired it, the interior was converted for administrative use in 1948. Today it holds the Alumni office and administrative offices.
Eberhardt Hall was added to the National Register of Historic Places on June 19, 1973.

eras.details: A new Gothic Victorian building with castle-like towers, the Newark Orphan Asylum, children in 1850s clothing on the lawn, gas lamps.

eras.caption: The college turns the old asylum into offices.
eras.details: The same Gothic castle-like building, now college offices in 1948, students in late-1940s clothing, 1940s cars on the street.

eras.caption: Eberhardt Hall today, and me beside it.
eras.details: The same Gothic castle-like building today, restored, with a mature oak tree beside it and modern students walking past.
